review_notes:
I read the whole file and grepped Mathlib for uses of `DFinsupp.singleton`, `rangeIcc`, `Finset.dfinsupp` and `DFinsupp.pi`. The only uses are inside this file, plus the parallel `Mathlib/Data/Finsupp/Interval.lean`. The candidates were:
- `Finset.dfinsupp`: a Finset-valued product construction. It has no homomorphism, continuity or action structure to bundle. Its useful structure is the membership and cardinality lemmas, and those are already stated.
- `DFinsupp.singleton`: this is pointwise `{f i}` and could be written with `DFinsupp.mapRange` and `Finset.singletonMonoidHom` (in `Mathlib/Algebra/Group/Pointwise/Finset/Basic.lean`). That would only reuse an existing combinator. Nothing else in Mathlib consumes `singleton`, so a bundled version would have no existing consumer.
- `rangeIcc`: a binary map into `Π₀ i, Finset (α i)`. It has no algebraic structure, because `Icc` is not additive or multiplicative.
- `instLocallyFiniteOrder`: this is already a bundled instance.
I found no case where structure is exposed only as separate facts and a standard bundle with a real consumer would improve the interface. I could not run Lean, so I did not test any alternative construction.
